definition_zh: n. 争论，争执；主张，论点；竞争
definition_en: disagreement, a claim, or a chance of winning
core_image: 两个人同时按住同一份文件，各说各的理
scene: 律师们围绕一个条款吵得面红耳赤。The lawyers were locked in contention over one clause.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：contention 指争论；句意是律师们围绕一个条款争执不下。

senses.title: Dispute
senses.definition: angry disagreement between people
senses.definitionCN: 人们之间的激烈分歧
senses.example: The project stirred up fierce contention.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目激起了激烈的争论。
senses.why: The noun of contending in words.
senses.whyCN: contend 用言语相争的名词形式。

senses.title: A claim
senses.definition: a statement that someone argues for
senses.definitionCN: 某人坚持的论点
senses.example: Her main contention is that the fee is too high.
senses.exampleCN: 她的主要主张是费用过高。
senses.why: One side stretches a point to win.
senses.whyCN: 一方为了取胜把观点拉长。

senses.title: Disputed point
senses.definition: the particular matter people disagree about
senses.definitionCN: 人们意见不一的具体事项
senses.example: Cost remains the bone of contention.
senses.exampleCN: 成本仍是争执的焦点。
senses.why: Bones are what dogs fight over.
senses.whyCN: 骨头正是狗争夺的东西。

senses.title: Competitive position
senses.definition: the position of competing for a prize
senses.definitionCN: 争夺奖项的位置
senses.example: The club is in contention for the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部有望争夺奖杯。
senses.why: Runners still in the race are in contention.
senses.whyCN: 仍在赛道上的选手才算在竞争行列。

intro.en: Contention comes from Latin contendere, to strain against.
intro.cn: contention 来自拉丁语 contendere，意为用力相抗。

items.en: Contendere means to strain or strive against.
items.cn: contendere 意为用力相争。

items.en: Contentio names a straining and a dispute.
items.cn: contentio 指紧绷与争执。

items.en: Old French contencion brought the quarrel sense.
items.cn: 古法语 contencion 带来争吵之义。

items.en: English used contention for disputes and claims.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语用它指争执与主张。

items.en: Sports writing uses it for a title race.
items.cn: 现代体育写作用它指争冠形势。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by a few letters; the near-meaning group names kinds of disagreement.
note.cn: 形近组只差几个字母；近义组列出各类分歧。

definition_zh: adj. 爱争论的；有争议的
definition_en: liking to argue, or likely to cause disagreement
core_image: 一个人举着手指在桌边与人争辩
scene: 这份有争议的提案让会场立刻吵了起来。The contentious proposal set the hall arguing at once.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：contentious 指有争议的；句意是这份提案让会场立刻吵起来。

senses.title: Fond of arguing
senses.definition: eager to argue about almost anything
senses.definitionCN: 几乎什么事都要争一争
senses.example: He is a contentious neighbour.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个爱吵架的邻居。
senses.why: Someone always ready to push back.
senses.whyCN: 总想顶回去的人。

senses.title: Causing disagreement
senses.definition: likely to start an argument

senses.example: Land rights remain contentious.
senses.exampleCN: 土地权问题仍很有争议。
senses.why: A match struck near dry grass.
senses.whyCN: 在干草边划着的火柴。

senses.title: In a legal dispute
senses.definition: relating to a formal dispute
senses.definitionCN: 与正式纠纷有关的
senses.example: The case was contentious from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 这场官司从一开始就有争议。
senses.why: Courtrooms are built for arguments.
senses.whyCN: 法庭本就是为争辩而设。

normalIntro.cn: contentious 就是随时准备顶回去。

definition_zh: 背景；上下文；语境
definition_en: the situation or the words around something that help explain it
core_image: 一段话的左右两边，把中间那句托住
scene: 读到生词时，她先把整段话看一遍再猜意思。You can guess the word from its context.
sceneCN: 这里 context 指「上下文」（第 1 个义项：词语前后相连的文字）；句意是你可以从上下文猜出这个词的意思。

senses.title: Surrounding words
senses.definition: the words before and after a word that help fix its meaning
senses.definitionCN: 位于某词前后、帮助确定其含义的文字
senses.example: Read the whole sentence to get the context.
senses.exampleCN: 读整个句子来把握上下文。
senses.why: A word alone can point several ways, and its neighbours steady it.
senses.whyCN: 一个词单看可以有几种指向，邻居让它稳住。

senses.title: The situation around
senses.definition: the conditions and events that surround something
senses.definitionCN: 围绕某事的条件与事件
senses.example: The decision made sense in the context of that year.
senses.exampleCN: 放在那一年的背景下，这个决定是说得通的。
senses.why: Nothing happens in empty air, and the air explains it.
senses.whyCN: 没有事发生在真空里，周围的空气正好解释它。

senses.title: Setting for meaning
senses.definition: the general field in which an idea is understood
senses.definitionCN: 理解某个观念所依托的整体领域
senses.example: The word has a different force in a legal context.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词在法律语境里力度不同。
senses.why: The same sentence changes colour when the room around it changes.
senses.whyCN: 同一句话，周围的房间一换，颜色也变了。

intro.en: Context comes from Latin contexere, to weave together, built from com-, together, and texere, to weave.
intro.cn: context 来自拉丁语 contexere，意为编织在一起，由 com-（一起）与 texere（编织）构成。

items.en: Texere meant to weave cloth from separate threads.
items.cn: texere 意为把分开的线织成布。

items.en: Contexere meant to weave things into one joined whole.
items.cn: contexere 意为把事物织成一个相连的整体。

items.en: Contextus named the joining of a text as well as a fabric.
items.cn: contextus 既指织物的连接，也指文字的连缀。

items.en: French contexte named the connected body of a written work.
items.cn: 法语 contexte 指一篇文字相连的整体。

items.en: English context first meant the words around a passage.
items.cn: 英语 context 最初指一段话周围的文字。

items.en: The word has widened to mean any surrounding situation.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩大为指任何周围的处境。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin weaving base text-, and the meaning group names other ways of speaking about surroundings.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的编织词基 text-，近义组列出其他表示周边环境的说法。

entries.definition: connected with the situation around something
the written words of a book or message
a false reason given to hide the real one
the conditions that come before and around an event
the place and conditions in which something happens
a fact or condition that affects a situation

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from words woven around a line, then move to the year around a choice and to the field around an idea.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从围绕一句话织起的词开始，再到围绕一个选择的年份，最后到围绕一个观念的领域。

normal.en: Con- is together and text is woven words, so context is words woven around a word.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，text 是织成的文字，context 就是围绕一个词织起来的文字。

normal.en: Pull one sentence out of the page and it may read wrongly.
normal.cn: 把一句话从页面里抽出来，它可能就读歪了。

normal.en: The same word is warm in one letter and cold in another.
normal.cn: 同一个词在一封信里是暖的，在另一封信里是冷的。

normal.en: Ask what was happening that year before you judge the choice.
normal.cn: 判断那个选择之前，先问那一年正在发生什么。

normal.en: A frame tells you how to see the picture inside it.
normal.cn: 画框会告诉你该怎么看框里的画。

abstract.en: Picture threads running in and out of one bright strand.
abstract.cn: 想象许多线在一根亮线两侧穿进穿出。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp lighting the wall behind a small object.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照亮小物件背后的墙面。

abstract.en: Picture a map with one red point and a wide pale field.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上有一个红点和一大片浅色区域。

examples.en: You can often guess a new word from its context.
examples.cn: 你常常能从上下文猜出一个新词的意思。

examples.en: The remark was harmless in context.
examples.cn: 这句话放在上下文里并无恶意。

examples.en: We need to see the plan in its historical context.
examples.cn: 我们需要把这项计划放回历史背景中看。

intro.en: Contiguous attaches the prefix con- to the root tangere, to touch.
intro.cn: contiguous 把前缀 con- 接在表「触摸」的词根 tangere 上。

latinIntro.en: Latin contiguus means touching or neighbouring.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 contiguus 意为相接的、邻近的。

definition_zh: 大洲；大陆
definition_en: one of the large separate areas of land on earth, or the main land apart from its islands
core_image: 一块被海水围住的巨大陆地，边缘被浪画出线
scene: 地图摊开，老师指着最大的一片陆地说出名字。Africa is the second largest continent.
sceneCN: 这里 continent 指「大洲」（第 1 个义项：地球上彼此分开的巨大陆地区域）；句意是非洲是面积第二大的洲。

senses.title: A great landmass
senses.definition: one of the large areas of land that the earth is divided into
senses.definitionCN: 地球上被划分出来的几块巨大陆地区域之一
senses.example: Asia is the largest continent.
senses.exampleCN: 亚洲是最大的洲。
senses.why: The sea draws the border that makes a continent one thing.
senses.whyCN: 海画出的边界，让一片陆地成为一个整体。

senses.title: The mainland
senses.definition: the main continuous land, as opposed to nearby islands
senses.definitionCN: 与附近岛屿相对的主要连片陆地
senses.example: The ferry links the island to the continent.
senses.exampleCN: 渡船把小岛与大陆连起来。
senses.why: An island sees the mainland as one big neighbour.
senses.whyCN: 岛屿把大陆看成一个巨大的邻居。

intro.en: Continent comes from Latin continens, continuous or holding together, from continere, to hold together, built from com-, together, and tenere, to hold.
intro.cn: continent 来自拉丁语 continens（连绵不断、连在一起），源于 continere（保持在一起），由 com-（一起）与 tenere（握住）构成。

items.en: Tenere meant to hold or keep in the hand.
items.cn: tenere 意为握住或保持在手中。

items.en: Continere meant to hold things together as one.
items.cn: continere 意为把事物保持为一个整体。

items.en: Continens described land that runs on without a break.
items.cn: continens 形容连绵不断、没有中断的陆地。

items.en: The noun terra continens, the continuous land, was shortened in use.
items.cn: 短语 terra continens（连成一片的陆地）在使用中被省略。

items.en: English continent named the great landmasses of the globe.
items.cn: 英语 continent 指地球上的几块巨大陆地。

items.en: It also means the mainland seen from an island.
items.cn: 它也表示从岛屿看去的大陆。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin holding base tin-, and the meaning group names other words for large pieces of land.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的握持词基 tin-，近义组列出其他表示大片陆地的词。

entries.definition: belonging to a continent
to keep going without stopping
to have something inside
the main land of a country, not its islands
a very large area of land
a large area of a country or the world

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from land held together by the sea, then move to the mainland seen from an island.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被海围住、连成一片的陆地开始，再到从岛上望见的大陆。

normal.en: Con- is together and tin is hold, so a continent is land held together.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，tin 是握住，continent 就是被握在一起的一片陆地。

normal.en: Pour blue water around a brown shape and you have made the word.
normal.cn: 在褐色地块周围倒上一圈蓝色，你就造出了这个词。

normal.en: A continent is big enough that you forget its edges.
normal.cn: 大陆大到你会忘记它的边缘。

normal.en: From a small island, the mainland is simply the continent.
normal.cn: 从小岛望去，本土就是大陆。

normal.en: Seven great pieces, one round globe.
normal.cn: 七块巨大的陆地，一个圆圆的地球。

abstract.en: Picture a brown shape with a thin white line of surf.
abstract.cn: 想象一块褐色陆地，边上镶着一线白浪。

abstract.en: Picture a ferry crossing a grey strait toward a wide shore.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘渡船穿过灰色海峡，驶向宽阔的海岸。

abstract.en: Picture a globe turned slowly until one mass fills the view.
abstract.cn: 想象地球缓缓转动，直到一整块陆地占满视野。

examples.en: The continent is rich in minerals.
examples.cn: 这片大陆矿产丰富。

examples.en: Few birds cross the whole continent.
examples.cn: 很少有鸟飞越整片大陆。

examples.en: Storms moved slowly across the continent.
examples.cn: 风暴缓缓扫过大陆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 continent 记成 con（一起）加 tin（握住）：一大片土地被海围住、始终连在一起，就是大陆。

root: 源自拉丁语 continens（连绵不断的），来自 continere（保持在一起），由 con-（一起）与 tenere（握住）构成。

sensesIntro.en: From one great land held together by the sea, to the mainland that an island looks toward.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被海围住的巨大陆块，到岛屿所遥望的大陆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brown landmass ringed by one thin line of surf.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块褐色陆地，被一线白浪围住。

branches.en: The largest division of land gets its own name.
branches.cn: 最大的一级陆地区域有了自己的名字。

branches.en: An island measures itself against the mainland.
branches.cn: 岛屿以大陆为参照来衡量自己。

branches.en: Both senses rest on land that holds together.
branches.cn: 两个义项都立足于连成一片的陆地。

branches.en: A continent is defined by the water around it.
branches.cn: 大洲由它周围的水来界定。

branches.en: The mainland is a continent seen from a smaller shore.
branches.cn: 大陆是从较小海岸望去的大洲。

intro.cn: continent 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 tenere（握住）构成。

latinIntro.en: The holding base ten- also appears in contain, retain and tenant.
latinIntro.cn: 握持词基 ten- 也出现在 contain、retain 与 tenant 中。

definition_zh: 大陆的；大陆性的；欧洲大陆的；北美殖民地的
definition_en: relating to a continent, especially to the mainland of Europe or to continental climate
core_image: 一整块连成一片的陆地，与周围被海水隔开的岛屿形成对照
scene: 两大板块相撞之后，地壳被挤压得又厚又高。The collision built a high plateau where continental crust had thickened.
sceneCN: 这里 continental 指「大陆的」（第 1 个义项：与大陆地壳有关的）；句意为碰撞在陆壳增厚处抬升出一片高高原。

pos.zh: 大陆的；大陆性的；欧洲大陆的；（北美历史）大陆军的

derivatives.zh: 大陆性（气候远离海洋的程度）

senses.title: Relating to a continent
senses.definition: relating to a continent or to the mainland rather than to islands
senses.definitionCN: 与大陆或本土有关的，而非与岛屿有关的
senses.example: The collision built a high plateau where continental crust had thickened.
senses.exampleCN: 碰撞在陆壳增厚处抬升出一片高高原。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun continent to whatever it describes, so continental crust is the crust that belongs to a continent.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词就是把名词 continent 挂到所修饰的对象上，所以大陆地壳就是属于大陆的地壳。

senses.title: Mainland Europe
senses.definition: in British usage, relating to the mainland of Europe
senses.definitionCN: 在英式用法中，与欧洲大陆有关的
senses.example: They spent the summer travelling on the continental side of the Channel.
senses.exampleCN: 他们夏天在海峡对岸的欧洲大陆旅行。
senses.why: From an island's viewpoint, 'the continent' is the nearest mainland, so continental means European in British speech.
senses.whyCN: 从岛屿的视角看，「大陆」就是最近的那块本土，所以英式口语中 continental 就指欧洲大陆的。

senses.title: Continental climate
senses.definition: describing a climate with hot summers and cold winters far from the sea
senses.definitionCN: 描述远离海洋、夏热冬冷的气候
senses.example: Continental interiors swing from hot summers to freezing winters.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆内部从炎夏摆到严寒的冬天。
senses.why: Land heats and cools faster than water, so places far inside a continent have a wider yearly range.
senses.whyCN: 陆地比水体升温降温更快，所以深入大陆内部的地区年温差更大。

senses.title: Relating to the continental shelf
senses.definition: describing the shallow sea floor that extends from a coast
senses.definitionCN: 描述从海岸延伸出去的浅海底
senses.example: Continental shelf waters support most of the world's fisheries.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆架水域支撑着世界大部分的渔业。
senses.why: The shelf is submerged continental crust, so the adjective marks it as part of the continent rather than the deep ocean.
senses.whyCN: 大陆架是被海水淹没的大陆地壳，因此这个形容词标明它属于大陆而不是深海。

senses.title: The American colonial sense
senses.definition: relating to the American colonies, as in the Continental Army
senses.definitionCN: 与美国殖民地有关的，如大陆军
senses.example: The Continental Congress met in Philadelphia.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆会议在费城召开。
senses.why: The colonies called the shared landmass 'the continent', so their army and congress took the name.
senses.whyCN: 各殖民地把自己所在的共同陆地称为「大陆」，因此他们的大陆军与大陆会议就用了这个名字。

senses.title: Relating to continental plates
senses.definition: describing the thick, buoyant parts of the crust that carry land
senses.definitionCN: 描述承载陆地、厚而轻的地壳部分
senses.example: Continental lithosphere floats higher than oceanic lithosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆岩石圈比大洋岩石圈浮得更高。
senses.why: Continental crust is less dense, so it rides high and cannot easily be subducted.
senses.whyCN: 大陆地壳密度较小，因此浮得高，也不容易被俯冲带走。

senses.title: Continental style
senses.definition: describing European habits of food, dress or daily life
senses.definitionCN: 描述欧洲的饮食、穿着或日常习惯
senses.example: The cafe serves a continental breakfast of bread and coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆供应面包配咖啡的欧陆式早餐。
senses.why: The label marks a style as coming from the mainland rather than from British practice.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签标明某种风格来自欧洲大陆，而不是英国本土的做法。

senses.title: Relating to continental law
senses.definition: describing the European legal tradition based on written codes
senses.definitionCN: 描述以成文法典为基础的欧洲法律传统
senses.example: Continental law relies on written codes more than on case precedent.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆法系更依赖成文法典，而不是判例。
senses.why: Legal systems differ by region, so continental marks the code-based tradition of mainland Europe.
senses.whyCN: 法律体系按地区不同，因此 continental 标记欧洲大陆以法典为基础的传统。

intro.en: Continental is the adjective of continent, from Latin continens 'holding together'. The word began as a description of continuous land and later acquired political and climatic senses. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: continental 是 continent 的形容词，源自拉丁语 continens「连在一起」。这个词最初描述连续的陆地，后来获得政治与气候义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Continens is the present participle of continere 'to hold together, contain', built from com- 'together' plus tenere 'to hold'.
items.cn: continens 是 continere「连在一起、容纳」的现在分词，由 com-「共同」加 tenere「握住」构成。

items.en: Terra continens meant 'continuous land', land not broken by sea, which is how the noun continent began.
items.cn: terra continens 意为「连续的陆地」，即未被海水分隔的陆地，名词 continent 就是由此而来。

items.en: Old French continental and English continental kept the sense 'belonging to a continent', first as a geographic description.
items.cn: 古法语 continental 与英语 continental 保留了「属于大陆的」这一义，最初是地理描述。

items.en: British speakers narrowed 'the Continent' to mainland Europe, so continental gained the sense 'European'.
items.cn: 英式使用者把 the Continent 缩小为欧洲大陆，于是 continental 获得了「欧洲的」这一义。

items.en: The American colonies used continental for their shared landmass, producing the Continental Congress and Continental Army.
items.cn: 北美殖民地用 continental 指他们共同的陆地，于是有了大陆会议与大陆军。

items.en: Geology added continental crust, continental shelf and continental drift, all built on the same 'continuous land' idea.
items.cn: 地质学增加了大陆地壳、大陆架与大陆漂移等说法，全部建立在同一个「连续陆地」观念上。

note.en: Group one holds words whose spelling or sound is close to continental; group two holds adjectives that also describe land on a large scale.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写或读音接近 continental 的词；第二组是同样描述大尺度陆地的形容词。

entries.definition: the noun meaning a large landmass; continental is its adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 表示大块陆地的名词；continental 是它的形容词。

entries.definition: happening repeatedly over time; it comes from continue, not from continent.
entries.definitionCN: 在时间上反复发生的；它来自 continue，而不是 continent。

entries.definition: going on without a break; it describes time or space, not a landmass.
entries.definitionCN: 不中断地持续；它描述时间或空间，不描述陆地。

entries.definition: touching along a border; it describes adjacency, not a continent.
entries.definitionCN: 沿边界相接的；它描述相邻关系，不指大陆。

entries.definition: the main land area of a country or region, as opposed to its islands.
entries.definitionCN: 一国或一地区的主要陆地区域，相对于其岛屿而言。

entries.definition: away from the coast; it describes position, not political or climatic style.
entries.definitionCN: 远离海岸的；它描述位置，而非政治或气候风格。

entries.definition: relating to Europe; it covers the British sense of continental but not the geological ones.
entries.definitionCN: 与欧洲有关的；它覆盖 continental 的英式义，但不覆盖地质义。

entries.definition: a very large continuous area of land; it is the thing continental describes.
entries.definitionCN: 极大的一片连续陆地；它是 continental 所描述的对象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real derivatives and real geographic contrasts, so the adjective is tied to the noun it modifies.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的派生词与真实的地理对照，因此这个形容词紧扣它所修饰的名词。

normal.en: continental is just continent plus -al: the adjective adds 'relating to' to the noun.
normal.cn: continental 就是 continent 加 -al：形容词给名词加上「与……有关」的意思。

normal.en: Continental crust is thick and light, which is why continents ride high above the ocean floor.
normal.cn: 大陆地壳又厚又轻，所以大陆高高地浮在洋底之上。

normal.en: A continental climate is one far from the sea, with hot summers and cold winters.
normal.cn: 大陆性气候就是远离海洋、夏热冬冷的气候。

normal.en: In British English, continental often just means European, as in a continental breakfast.
normal.cn: 在英式英语中，continental 常常就指欧洲的，比如欧陆式早餐。

normal.en: The Continental Congress took its name from the shared North American landmass.
normal.cn: 大陆会议的名字来自北美各殖民地共享的那块陆地。

abstract.en: Abstractly, continental means 'belonging to the big continuous block', as opposed to the fragment or the island.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，continental 表示「属于连成一片的大块」，与碎片或岛屿相对。

abstract.en: The word always measures scale: what counts as the mainland depends on where the speaker stands.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终在衡量尺度：什么算「大陆」，取决于说话人站在哪里。

abstract.en: Symbol: one large continuous shape and three small detached dots beside it.
abstract.cn: 符号：一个连成一片的大块，旁边三个分离的小点。

examples.en: Continental crust is older and thicker than oceanic crust.
examples.cn: 大陆地壳比大洋地壳更古老、更厚。

examples.en: The interior has a harsh continental climate.
examples.cn: 内陆地区是严酷的大陆性气候。

examples.en: They took a train across continental Europe.
examples.cn: 他们乘火车穿越欧洲大陆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「康提南头」—— 一块连成一片的大陆地伸到南头 → continental 大陆的

root: 源自拉丁语 continens（连在一起的陆地），由 com-（共同）加 tenere（握住）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of continental. They all point to one large continuous landmass, whether the context is geology, climate, Europe or American history.
sensesIntro.cn: continental 的八个义项都指向同一块连成一片的大陆地，无论语境是地质、气候、欧洲还是美国历史。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one large continuous land block, opposed to islands and fragments.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块连成一片的大陆地，与岛屿和碎片相对。

branches.en: LAND AND SHELF: the same continent continues under shallow sea.
branches.cn: 陆地与陆架：同一块大陆在浅海之下继续延伸。

branches.en: MAINLAND STYLE: from an island, the mainland means Europe in food, habit and law.
branches.cn: 大陆风格：从岛屿看，大陆在饮食、习惯与法律上都指欧洲。

branches.en: CLIMATE: distance from the sea makes the yearly range wider.
branches.cn: 气候：离海越远，年温差越大。

branches.en: CRUST: thick light rock makes continents float high.
branches.cn: 地壳：厚而轻的岩石使大陆浮得高。

branches.en: HISTORY: the colonies named their shared land the continent.
branches.cn: 历史：各殖民地把自己共享的陆地称为大陆。

intro.en: Continental is the adjective built on continent with -al, and the same pattern produces several compounds about crossing or belonging to continents.
intro.cn: continental 是由 continent 加 -al 构成的形容词，同一模式还产生若干表示「跨越大陆」或「属于次大陆」的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is continere 'to hold together' (com- + tenere); continens and the adjective continentalis pass into English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 continere「连在一起」（com- + tenere）；continens 与形容词 continentalis 经法语进入英语。

items.example: The Latin verb supplies the 'continuous' idea.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词提供了「连续」的意思。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词。

items.example: The continent stretches from ocean to ocean.
items.exampleCN: 这块大陆从一个大洋延伸到另一个大洋。

items.meaning: the degree to which a place is far from the sea
items.meaningCN: 某地远离海洋的程度（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.exampleCN: 大陆性提高了夏季温度。

items.example: A transcontinental railway linked the two coasts.
items.exampleCN: 一条横贯大陆的铁路连接了两岸。

items.example: The subcontinental shelf is unusually wide.
items.exampleCN: 这个次大陆的陆架异常宽阔。

items.meaning: the shallow sea floor next to a continent
items.example: The continental shelf is rich in fish.

latinEntries.meaningCN: 连在一起的；连续的陆地

definition_zh: n. 可能发生的意外；应急方案；偶然性
definition_en: a possible future event, or a plan for one
core_image: 抽屉里备着一只手电筒，等停电时用
scene: 预算里留出一成资金，用来应付意外。The plan keeps a tenth of the budget for contingencies.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：contingency 指可能发生的意外；句意是预算留钱应付意外。

pos.zh: 意外情况；应急方案；偶然性

senses.title: A possible event
senses.definition: something that may happen but is not certain
senses.definitionCN: 可能发生但不确定的事
senses.example: Bad weather is a contingency we must plan for.
senses.exampleCN: 坏天气是我们必须准备的意外。
senses.why: A branch on a path that may be taken.
senses.whyCN: 路上可能走的一条岔路。

senses.title: A backup plan
senses.definition: arrangements made in case something happens
senses.definitionCN: 为防万一而做的安排
senses.example: The team drew up a contingency.
senses.exampleCN: 团队拟好了一套应急方案。
senses.why: A spare key kept in a drawer.
senses.whyCN: 抽屉里备着的一把钥匙。

senses.title: Dependence on chance
senses.definition: the state of depending on chance
senses.definitionCN: 依赖机缘的状态
senses.example: The outcome has too much contingency.
senses.exampleCN: 结果太依赖偶然因素。
senses.why: Dice decide nothing in advance.
senses.whyCN: 骰子从不预先决定结果。

senses.title: An unforeseen cost
senses.definition: an extra expense no one predicted
senses.definitionCN: 没人预料到的额外支出
senses.example: A repair fund covers contingencies.
senses.exampleCN: 维修基金用来支付意外开支。
senses.why: A hole in the road costs money.

definition_zh: 继续；持续；延伸
definition_en: to keep doing something after a pause, to go on without stopping, or to stretch further
core_image: 一条路穿过田野，一直伸到看不见的地方
scene: 雨停了一会儿又下起来，队伍仍往前走。They decided to continue the march after a short rest.
sceneCN: 这里 continue 指「继续」（第 1 个义项：停顿之后接着做同一件事）；句意是他们决定稍作休息后继续行军。

senses.title: Keep doing
senses.definition: to go on with an activity after a short pause
senses.definitionCN: 短暂停顿之后接着做同一件事
senses.example: She continued her story after a sip of tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她喝了口茶，接着讲她的故事。
senses.why: A pause is not an ending, for the thread can be picked up again.
senses.whyCN: 停顿不是结束，线还能再捡起来。

senses.title: Go on without stopping
senses.definition: to last or keep happening without a break
senses.definitionCN: 不间断地延续或发生
senses.example: The rain continued all night.
senses.exampleCN: 雨下了一整夜。
senses.why: Some things have no clear edge where they might stop.
senses.whyCN: 有些事物没有明显的边可以让它停下。

senses.title: Stretch onward
senses.definition: to extend further in space
senses.definitionCN: 在空间上向前延伸
senses.example: The path continues beyond the hill.

senses.why: A line drawn on a map asks to be followed.
senses.whyCN: 地图上画出的线，总在请人跟着走。

intro.en: Continue comes from Latin continuare, to join together and carry on, from continuus, unbroken, and before that from continere, to hold together.
intro.cn: continue 来自拉丁语 continuare（连接起来、接着进行），源于 continuus（不间断的），更早出自 continere（保持在一起）。

items.en: Continere meant to hold things together in one piece.
items.cn: continere 意为把事物保持成一个整体。

items.en: Continuus meant hanging together with no break.
items.cn: continuus 意为连在一起而没有断开。

items.en: Continuare meant to make a thing go on further.
items.cn: continuare 意为使某事继续向前。

items.en: French continuer meant to carry on a begun action.
items.cn: 法语 continuer 意为把已开始的动作接着做下去。

items.en: English continue kept both the time and the space senses.
items.cn: 英语 continue 同时保留时间与空间两层意思。

items.en: It now covers pausing, lasting and stretching onward.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖停顿后继续、持续与向前延伸。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the nearest members of the continue family, and the meaning group names other verbs for going on.
note.cn: 形近组收的是 continue 词族里最容易混的几个词，近义组列出其他表示进行下去的动词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a thread taken up again, then move to rain that will not stop and a road that keeps going.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从重新捡起的线开始，再到停不下来的雨，最后到一直往前伸展的路。

normal.en: Con- is together and tin is hold, so continue is holding on to the same thread.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，tin 是握住，continue 就是一直握着同一条线。

normal.en: Put down the cup, pick up the sentence: that is the verb.
normal.cn: 放下杯子，重新拿起那句话：这就是这个动词。

normal.en: Rain does not need permission to keep falling.
normal.cn: 雨要继续下，并不需要谁的允许。

normal.en: A path that keeps going is doing the same word in space.

normal.en: Stop, breathe, then continue.

abstract.en: Picture a page turned, with the sentence running on.
abstract.cn: 想象翻过一页，句子仍在往下走。

abstract.en: Picture a road that narrows but never ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一条越来越窄却始终不结束的路。

examples.en: The meeting will continue after lunch.

examples.en: The valley continues for many miles.

root: 源自拉丁语 continuare（连接起来、接着进行），来自 continuus（不间断的）与 continere（保持在一起），指继续、持续与延伸。

sensesIntro.en: From picking up an action after a pause, to lasting without a break, and at last to stretching through space.
sensesIntro.cn: 从停顿后重新接上动作，到不间断地持续，最后到在空间中向前延伸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thread held in one hand that never leaves it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手握着线，始终没有松开。

branches.en: The first sense picks an action back up.
branches.cn: 第一个义项把动作重新捡起来。

branches.en: The second sense lets time run without a break.
branches.cn: 第二个义项让时间不间断地流。

branches.en: The third sense lays the same idea on the ground.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把同一个意思铺到地面上。

branches.en: Both senses share the refusal to end.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享不肯结束这一点。

branches.en: What lasts in time can also reach across space.
branches.cn: 在时间里延续的东西，也能横跨空间。

latinIntro.cn: 握持词基 tin- 也贯穿 continuous、continuity 与 contain。

definition_zh: 连续性；连贯；衔接；（电影）连贯性
definition_en: the state of continuing without interruption; the way in which things connect together without sudden changes; in film, the consistency of details between shots
core_image: 一条线从一头拉到另一头，中间没有断开
scene: 这组词中，To ensure continuity in the story, the author kept the same narrator throughout the novel.
sceneCN: 这里 continuity 是「连贯性」（第 1 个义项：不间断的状态）；句意：为了保证故事的连贯性，作者在整部小说中保持同一个叙述者。图中可辨识物件：书本、钢笔、一条贯穿的线、人物剪影。

senses.title: The state of continuing without interruption
senses.definition: the state of continuing for a period of time without stopping or being interrupted
senses.definitionCN: 持续一段时间而不停顿或中断的状态
senses.example: The continuity of the music was broken by a sudden crash.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐的连续性被突然的碎裂声打断。
senses.why: Latin continere 'to hold together': continuity is the state of being held together as one unbroken thing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 continere「保持在一起」：continuity 是作为一个未断整体保持在一起的状态。

senses.title: Logical connection between parts
senses.definition: the way in which the parts of something connect together logically and consistently
senses.definitionCN: 某物各部分逻辑一致地连接在一起的方式
senses.example: There is a clear continuity between his early and late work.
senses.exampleCN: 他的早期和晚期作品之间有明显的连贯性。
senses.why: When ideas connect smoothly, the 'thread' holds them together in continuity.
senses.whyCN: 当观念顺畅连接时，「线」把它们保持在 continuity 中。

senses.title: Uninterrupted succession
senses.definition: an uninterrupted sequence or succession of things
senses.definitionCN: 事物不间断的序列或接续
senses.example: The team achieved a continuity of victories last season.
senses.exampleCN: 该队上赛季取得了连胜。
senses.why: Here continuity is a series of events with no gap between them.
senses.whyCN: 此处 continuity 是事件之间没有间隙的系列。

senses.title: Consistency of details in film
senses.definition: in film and television, the consistency of details such as props and costumes between shots
senses.definitionCN: 影视中，镜头之间道具、服装等细节的一致性
senses.example: The script supervisor is responsible for continuity.
senses.exampleCN: 场记负责镜头间的连贯性。
senses.why: In film, continuity keeps the fictional world from breaking when the camera cuts.
senses.whyCN: 在电影中，continuity 保证镜头切换时虚构世界不穿帮。

senses.title: Maintenance of an unbroken flow
senses.definition: the maintenance of an unbroken flow or operation, especially in business
senses.definitionCN: 尤指业务中保持不间断的流程或运转
senses.example: The company has a business continuity plan for emergencies.
senses.exampleCN: 公司有应对紧急情况的业务连续性计划。
senses.why: Business continuity means the operation keeps going even when disrupted.
senses.whyCN: 业务连续性意味着即使受到干扰，运营也能持续。

senses.title: A link connecting different periods
senses.definition: a feature or relationship that connects one period or stage to another
senses.definitionCN: 把一个时期或阶段与另一个连接起来的特征或关系
senses.example: The castle provides continuity between medieval and modern times.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城堡提供了中世纪与现代之间的衔接。
senses.why: Something that bridges two eras gives continuity of experience or memory.
senses.whyCN: 跨越两个时代的事物提供了经验或记忆的衔接。

senses.title: Mathematical property of functions
senses.definition: in mathematics, the property of a function whose graph has no breaks or jumps
senses.definitionCN: 数学中，函数图像没有断裂或跳跃的性质
senses.example: Students learn about continuity in calculus.
senses.exampleCN: 学生在微积分中学习连续性。
senses.why: In math, a continuous function can be drawn without lifting the pencil — the line holds together.
senses.whyCN: 在数学中，连续函数可以一笔画成——线保持不断。

senses.title: Unbroken existence through time
senses.definition: the state of existing or remaining the same over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 在长时间内存在或保持不变的状态
senses.example: The family business has remarkable continuity over three centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这家家族企业三个世纪以来持续存在，令人瞩目。
senses.why: When an institution survives unchanged, it shows continuity across time.
senses.whyCN: 当一个机构不变地存续下来，它就展示了跨越时间的 continuity。

intro.en: Continuity comes from Latin continuitas, from continuus 'uninterrupted', from continere 'to hold together'. The core is one thing holding together without a break.
intro.cn: continuity 来自拉丁 continuitas，源自 continuus「不间断的」，continuus 来自 continere「保持在一起」。核心是一物保持不断。

items.en: continere is con- 'together' + tenere 'to hold'. It means 'to hold together, contain'.
items.cn: continere 是 con-「一起」+ tenere「握住」。意为「保持在一起、容纳」。

items.en: continuus meant 'uninterrupted, continuous' — what holds together as one piece.
items.cn: continuus 意为「不间断的、连续的」——作为一块保持在一起的。

items.en: continuitas meant 'uninterrupted connection or succession'. It was borrowed into French and English.
items.cn: continuitas 意为「不间断的连接或接续」。它被借入法语和英语。

items.en: Continuity entered English in the 15th century from French continuité.
items.cn: continuity 在 15 世纪从法语 continuité 进入英语。

items.en: The mathematical sense developed in the 17th century; the film sense in the 20th.
items.cn: 数学义发展于 17 世纪；电影义发展于 20 世纪。

items.en: Today continuity appears in business, broadcasting, mathematics, and everyday talk about connection.
items.cn: 如今 continuity 出现在商业、广播、数学以及关于连接的日常谈论中。

note.en: The first group shares tenere; the second contains words near in meaning of connection or consistency.
note.cn: 第一组共享 tenere；第二组是连接或一致意义相近的词。

normal.en: contain uses the same root: holding things inside.

normal.en: In film, continuity means nothing changes between shots — the story holds together.
normal.cn: 在电影中，continuity 意味着镜头之间没有变化——故事保持连贯。

abstract.en: Think of drawing a line without lifting your pen: that line is continuity.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔画成一条线：这条线就是 continuity。

abstract.en: Think of a bridge spanning a river: it gives continuity between the two banks.
abstract.cn: 想象一座横跨河流的桥：它提供了两岸之间的连续性。

abstract.en: Think of a movie where a cup is full in one shot and empty in the next without explanation: that's broken continuity.
abstract.cn: 想象一部电影，一个镜头里杯子是满的，下一个镜头里却空了而没有交代：这就是连续性断裂。

examples.en: There needs to be continuity between the old policy and the new one.
examples.cn: 新旧政策之间需要有连续性。

examples.en: The director fired the continuity clerk for missing a costume error.
examples.cn: 导演因场记漏看服装错误而解雇了她。

examples.en: The function has no continuity at this point because it jumps.
examples.cn: 该函数在这一点不连续，因为它发生了跳跃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「康提牛阿提」——康师傅提（tenere）着牛一路走，没断开 → continuity 连续性

root: 拉丁 continere「保持在一起、容纳」（con-「一起」+ tenere「握住」）；continuus 形容词 + -ity 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all mean 'holding together without a break': a story, a business, a film's details, or a mathematical line.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都表示「不断地保持在一起」：故事、业务、电影细节或数学线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unbroken line drawn in one stroke.
core.cn: 核心意象：一笔画成的不间断的线。

branches.en: UNBROKEN SEQUENCE: events or states continuing without a gap.
branches.cn: 不间断序列：事件或状态无间隙地持续。

branches.en: CONNECTION ACROSS PARTS OR TIMES: a link that holds parts or eras together.
branches.cn: 跨部分或跨时代的连接：把部分或时代保持在一起的纽带。

branches.en: FILM CONTINUITY: consistent details between shots.
branches.cn: 电影连贯性：镜头间一致的细节。

branches.en: DURABLE OPERATION OR EXISTENCE: something that keeps going through time.
branches.cn: 持久的运转或存在：穿越时间持续的事物。

branches.en: MATHEMATICAL CONTINUITY: a function with no jumps or breaks.
branches.cn: 数学连续性：没有跳跃或断裂的函数。

intro.en: Continuity is the -ity noun from continuous, from Latin continuus. The suffix -ity is productive; the inner parts are fossilized.
intro.cn: continuity 是 continuous 的 -ity 名词，continuous 来自拉丁 continuus。后缀 -ity 有能产性；内部部分已凝固。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere 'to hold' produced a huge family: contain, retain, maintain, detain, sustain, obtain, continue. The root appears as ten-, tin-, tent-, or tain-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tenere「握住」产生了庞大家族：contain、retain、maintain、detain、sustain、obtain、continue。词根以 ten-、tin-、tent- 或 tain- 形式出现。

items.exampleCN: 数据中有一个不连续点。

definition_en: happening or existing without any break or gap
core_image: 一笔画到底的直线，中间没有断口

pos.zh: 连续的；不间断的；连绵的

senses.title: Without a break
senses.definition: going on with no pause or gap in time
senses.definitionCN: 在时间上进行中没有任何停顿或缺口
senses.example: A continuous line runs along the top of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 一条不断的线横贯页面顶端。
senses.why: The eye trusts a line that never lifts from the paper.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛信任一条始终没离开纸面的线。

senses.title: Unbroken in space
senses.definition: covering an area from end to end without gaps
senses.definitionCN: 在空间上从头到尾连成一片没有空隙
senses.example: A continuous wall surrounds the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 一道连绵的墙围着老城。
senses.why: No gate and no crack means the wall reads as one thing.
senses.whyCN: 没有门也没有裂缝，墙就读成一个整体。

senses.title: Steady in supply
senses.definition: provided at every moment over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内每一刻都得到供应
senses.example: The plant needs a continuous supply of cool air.
senses.exampleCN: 这座工厂需要持续的冷气供应。
senses.why: Some processes cannot wait for the next delivery.
senses.whyCN: 有些过程等不到下一批货。

intro.en: Continuous comes from Latin continuus, hanging together without a break, from continere, to hold together.
intro.cn: continuous 来自拉丁语 continuus（连在一起、不断开），源于 continere（保持在一起）。

items.en: Continere meant to keep parts in one unbroken whole.
items.cn: continere 意为把各部分保持在一个不断开的整体里。

items.en: Continuus described a line or period with no gap.
items.cn: continuus 形容没有缺口的线或时段。

items.en: The suffix -ous marked a quality in adjectives.
items.cn: 后缀 -ous 在形容词里表示某种性质。

items.en: French continu carried the same unbroken sense.
items.cn: 法语 continu 带有同样的不断义。

items.en: English continuous was used for time, space and motion.
items.cn: 英语 continuous 用于时间、空间与运动。

items.en: It is now carefully kept apart from continual.
items.cn: 如今它被小心地与 continual 区分开。

note.en: The look-alike group sets continuous against its closest relatives, and the meaning group names other words for what does not break.
note.cn: 形近组把 continuous 与最亲近的几个词放在一起，近义组列出其他表示不断开的词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a line that never lifts, then move to a wall without a gate and a supply that never waits.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从始终不抬起的线开始，再到没有门的墙，最后到等不得的供应。

normal.en: Continuous means no gap, while continual means many gaps.
normal.cn: continuous 是没有缺口，continual 是许多缺口。

normal.en: Draw one stroke across the page and do not lift the pen.
normal.cn: 在纸上一笔画过去，不要抬笔。

normal.en: A wall with no gate is continuous, and so is a hum with no pause.
normal.cn: 没有门的墙是不间断的，没有停顿的嗡嗡声也是。

normal.en: Think of a tap that never closes for an hour.
normal.cn: 想一想一只一小时都没关的水龙头。

normal.en: If you can point to a break, the word is not this one.
normal.cn: 只要你能指出一处中断，这个词就不适用。

abstract.en: Picture a single white stroke on a dark page.
abstract.cn: 想象深色纸面上只有一笔白线。

abstract.en: Picture a ribbon pulled tight with no knot.
abstract.cn: 想象一条拉紧、没有打结的丝带。

abstract.en: Picture a river that never shows a dry stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从不露出干石的河。

examples.en: The machine needs a continuous supply of water.
examples.cn: 这台机器需要持续供水。

examples.en: A continuous line of cars filled the road.
examples.cn: 一长串不断的车占满了路。

examples.en: The baby slept in a continuous stretch.
examples.cn: 婴儿一口气睡了很久没有醒。

sensesIntro.en: From time with no pause, to space with no gap, and at last to a supply that never stops arriving.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没有停顿的时间，到没有空隙的空间，最后到从不断供的供应。

branches.en: Space joins end to end in the second sense.

definition_zh: 合同；契约；收缩；染上（疾病）
definition_en: a written agreement between two sides, or to become smaller, or to catch an illness
core_image: 两双手在纸上按下印章，纸边向里卷起
scene: 签完字，双方各留一份，纸被折好放进公文包。Both sides signed the contract on Friday.
sceneCN: 这里 contract 指「合同」（第 1 个义项：双方签下的书面约定）；句意是双方在周五签了这份合同。

senses.title: A written agreement
senses.definition: a formal written promise made between two or more sides
senses.definitionCN: 两方或多方之间作出的正式书面承诺
senses.example: The contract runs for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这份合同为期两年。
senses.why: A promise on paper outlives the mood that made it.
senses.whyCN: 写在纸上的承诺，比许下它的心情活得更久。

senses.title: To draw smaller
senses.definition: to become shorter, narrower or tighter
senses.definitionCN: 变得更短、更窄或更紧
senses.example: Metal contracts as it cools.
senses.exampleCN: 金属冷却时会收缩。
senses.why: Cold pulls the pieces closer together.
senses.whyCN: 冷把各个部分拉得更近。

senses.title: To catch an illness
senses.definition: to begin to suffer from a disease
senses.definitionCN: 开始患上某种疾病
senses.example: He contracted a fever in the wet season.
senses.exampleCN: 他在雨季染上了热病。
senses.why: An illness can be picked up the way a habit is.
senses.whyCN: 疾病也能像习惯一样被沾染上身。

intro.en: Contract comes from Latin contrahere, to draw together, built from com-, together, and trahere, to draw or pull.
intro.cn: contract 来自拉丁语 contrahere（拉在一起），由 com-（一起）与 trahere（拉）构成。

items.en: Trahere meant to draw or pull something along.
items.cn: trahere 意为拖或拉某物。

items.en: Contrahere meant to pull parts into a smaller space.
items.cn: contrahere 意为把各部分拉进更小的空间。

items.en: The noun contractus named a drawing together, then a bargain.
items.cn: 名词 contractus 先指拉紧，后指订立的约定。

items.en: French contract named a formal agreement.
items.cn: 法语 contract 指正式的约定。

items.en: English contract kept both the agreement and the shrinking senses.
items.cn: 英语 contract 同时保留约定与收缩两层意思。

items.en: The illness sense grew from the idea of being drawn into.
items.cn: 染病义由被卷入其中的想法发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin drawing base tract-, and the meaning group names other words for agreements and shrinking.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的拉动词基 tract-，近义组列出其他表示约定与收缩的词。

senses.titleCN: 反驳：把对方的话反过来说
senses.definition: to state that what someone has just said is wrong, and give the opposite account
senses.definitionCN: 指出某人刚说的话是错的，并给出相反的说法
senses.example: She contradicted him in front of the whole committee.
senses.exampleCN: 她当着整个委员会的面反驳了他。
senses.why: Latin contra dicere is literally 'to speak against'. The word does not merely disagree; it places a second statement directly opposite the first.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 contra dicere 字面就是“反着说”。这个词不只是不同意，而是把第二句话直接放在第一句话的对面。

senses.title: Of statements: be inconsistent
senses.titleCN: 相互矛盾：两句话不能同时成立
senses.definition: of two statements or facts, to be incompatible so that both cannot be true at once
senses.definitionCN: （两句话或两个事实）互不相容，不能同时为真
senses.example: The two reports contradict each other on the date.
senses.exampleCN: 两份报告在日期上互相矛盾。
senses.why: When two statements are set opposite each other, there is no ground on which both can stand. This 'be inconsistent with' sense is recorded from about 1600.
senses.whyCN: 当两句话被放到彼此对面，就没有任何一块地面能让两者同时站住。这一“与……不一致”义约记录于 1600 年。

senses.title: Deny a claim or an accusation
senses.definition: to deny the truth of a claim, accusation or rumour
senses.definitionCN: 否认某项主张、指控或传闻的真实性
senses.example: The company contradicted the rumour of a merger.
senses.exampleCN: 公司否认了合并的传闻。
senses.why: The sense 'deny the words or assertions of' is recorded from about 1600. Denial is the negative half of speaking against.
senses.whyCN: “否认某人的话或断言”这一义项约记录于 1600 年。否认是“反着说”的否定那一半。

senses.title: Contradict oneself
senses.titleCN: 自相矛盾：自己前后打起来
senses.definition: to make two statements that cannot both be true, so that one cancels the other
senses.definitionCN: 说出两句不能同时为真的话，使一句抵消另一句
senses.example: He contradicted himself twice during the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 他在采访中两次自相矛盾。
senses.why: The reflexive form turns the opposition inward: the speaker is now both parties, and the two statements pull against each other inside one mouth.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式把对立转向内部：说话者现在同时是两方，两句话在同一张嘴里面互相拉扯。

senses.title: Contradictory: mutually opposed
senses.definition: the adjective describes two things that cannot both be true or both be accepted
senses.definitionCN: 形容词描述两件不能同时为真或同时被接受的事
senses.example: The witness gave two contradictory accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 证人给出了两份相互矛盾的陈述。
senses.why: The -ory suffix marks a relation of opposition: each item points away from the other, like the two arrows from one point.
senses.whyCN: -ory 后缀标记对立关系：两项各自背离对方，就像从同一点射出的两支反向箭头。

senses.title: Contradiction: the opposing statement
senses.definition: the noun for a statement that denies or opposes another statement
senses.definitionCN: 指否定或反对另一句话的那句陈述
senses.example: His calm reply was a contradiction of everything she had said.
senses.exampleCN: 他平静的回答是对她所说一切的否定。
senses.why: The -tion noun names the second statement itself. In logic it is the proposition that asserts the negation of another.
senses.whyCN: -tion 名词命名第二句话本身。在逻辑中，它就是断言另一命题之否定的那个命题。

senses.title: Contradiction in logic
senses.titleCN: 逻辑矛盾：同时肯定与否
senses.definition: in logic, the relation between a statement and its negation, which cannot both be true
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中一个命题与其否定之间的关系，两者不能同时为真
senses.example: The proof ends in a contradiction, so the assumption is false.
senses.exampleCN: 证明以矛盾收尾，所以那个假设是假的。
senses.why: Philosophy uses contradiction as a tool: if assuming P leads to P and not-P, then P must be rejected. Two arrows cannot both be the true direction.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把矛盾当作工具：若假设 P 会推出 P 与非 P，则 P 必须被否定。两支箭头不可能同时是正确方向。

senses.title: Contradict the evidence or the record
senses.definition: of a fact or statement, to be contrary to what the evidence or record shows
senses.definitionCN: （事实或陈述）与证据或记录所显示的内容相反
senses.example: His version of events contradicts the phone records.
senses.exampleCN: 他对事件的描述与通话记录相矛盾。
senses.why: Here the second party is not a person but a record. The record 'speaks' too, and the verb treats it as an opposing voice.
senses.whyCN: 这里的第二方不是人，而是一份记录。记录也会“说话”，动词把它当成一个对立的声音。

senses.title: Contradict the trend or expectation
senses.definition: to be contrary to a general pattern, expectation or rule, often surprisingly
senses.definitionCN: 与一般模式、预期或规则相反，常含出人意料之意
senses.example: The results contradict the usual pattern of growth.
senses.exampleCN: 这些结果与通常的增长模式相反。
senses.why: This extension drops the human speaker entirely: any fact can stand opposite a pattern, and the pattern is what is contradicted.
senses.whyCN: 这一延伸完全去掉了人类说话者：任何事实都能站在某个模式对面，而被反驳的是那个模式。

intro.en: Contradict comes from Latin contradicere, in classical Latin two words: contra 'against' + dicere 'to say, speak'. It is literally 'speak against', and its relatives dictation, predict and verdict all keep the 'say' root.
intro.cn: contradict 来自拉丁语 contradicere，在古典拉丁语中是两个词：contra“反对”加 dicere“说、讲”。它字面就是“反着说”，其亲属 dictation、predict、verdict 都保留“说”这个词根。

items.en: Contra dicere meant 'to speak against'. The prefix contra was originally a comparative form meaning 'in comparison with', which hardened into 'against, opposite'.
items.cn: contra dicere 意为“反着说”。前缀 contra 最初是比较级形式，意为“与……相比”，后来固化为“反对、相反”。

items.en: Dicere 'to say, speak' comes from PIE *deik- 'to show, pronounce solemnly'. The same root gives dictate, predict, verdict, diction and index.
items.cn: dicere“说、讲”来自原始印欧语 *deik-“显示、郑重宣告”。同一词根给出 dictate、predict、verdict、diction、index。

items.en: English recorded contradict in the 1570s meaning 'speak against, oppose' — a sense now obsolete.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪 70 年代记录 contradict，意为“反着说、反对”——这一义项现已废弃。

items.en: From the 1580s it meant 'assert the contrary or opposite of', which is the modern core.
items.cn: 自 16 世纪 80 年代起，它意为“断言相反或对立的一面”，这是现代的核心义。

items.en: Two senses appear around 1600: 'deny the words or assertions of' and, of statements, 'be inconsistent with'. The word moves from a person's speech to the relation between propositions.
items.cn: 约 1600 年出现两个义项：“否认某人的话或断言”，以及（就陈述而言）“与……不一致”。这个词从人的言语转向命题之间的关系。

items.en: Modern English keeps person-against-person (contradict a witness) and fact-against-fact (the data contradict the theory). Contradict is the only one of the con- verbs built on 'speak'.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留“人对人”（contradict a witness）与“事实对事实”（数据与理论相矛盾）。在 con- 系列动词里，contradict 是唯一建在“说”之上的。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the dicere root from two near-spellings; the near-meaning group ranks kinds of opposition from simple denial to logical refutation.
note.cn: 形近组把 dicere 词根与两个近形词分开；近义组按对立程度排列，从简单否认到逻辑反驳。

entries.definition: an agreement, or to shrink. Its root is trahere 'draw', so it means 'draw together', not 'speak against'.
entries.definitionCN: 协议，或收缩。它的词根是 trahere“拉”，所以是“拉到一起”，不是“反着说”。

entries.definition: to break a rule or law. Contra- 'against' + venire 'come' = come against, so it opposes a rule rather than a statement.
entries.definitionCN: 违反规则或法律。contra-“反对”加 venire“来”＝迎面而来，所以它反对的是规则，而不是陈述。

entries.definition: the way words are chosen and pronounced. It is the noun of dicere, the 'saying' side without contra-.
entries.definitionCN: 用词与发音的方式。它是 dicere 的名词，是“说”的一面，没有 contra-。

entries.definition: to state that something is not true. It is the simple negative act; contradict adds the opposing statement or the clash between two claims.
entries.definitionCN: 声称某事不真实。它是简单的否定行为；contradict 还加上“相反的说法”或“两种主张的冲突”。

entries.definition: to be against a plan, person or idea. It is broader and can be silent; contradict must be spoken or written.
entries.definitionCN: 反对计划、人或观念。它范围更广，可以不出声；contradict 必须说出或写出。

entries.definition: to prove a claim false with evidence. It is stronger than contradict, which only asserts the opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 用证据证明某主张为假。它比 contradict 更强，后者只是断言相反。

entries.definition: of facts, interests or statements, to be incompatible. It is the neutral verb for the clash, without the 'speaking' image.
entries.definitionCN: （事实、利益或陈述）互不相容。它是描述冲突的中性动词，没有“说话”的意象。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: contra 'against' + dicere 'say', the same-root family predict, dictate, verdict, diction, and the fixed phrase contradict oneself.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实构件：contra“反对”+ dicere“说”，同根词族 predict、dictate、verdict、diction，以及固定搭配 contradict oneself。

normal.en: Contra means 'against' and dicere means 'say'. To contradict is simply to say against.
normal.cn: contra 意为“反对”，dicere 意为“说”。contradict 就是“反着说”。

normal.en: Predict is 'say before', dictate is 'say for writing', and verdict is 'truly said'. All keep the dic- root.
normal.cn: predict 是“提前说”，dictate 是“说给别人写”，verdict 是“如实说出”。它们都保留 dic- 词根。

normal.en: Contradict, contract and contact look alike but rest on three roots: speak against (dicere), draw together (trahere), touch (tangere).
normal.cn: contradict、contract、contact 形似但立足三个词根：反着说（dicere）、拉到一起（trahere）、触碰（tangere）。

normal.en: Contradict oneself is the same opposition turned inward: you are both the speaker and the one spoken against.
normal.cn: contradict oneself 是同一个对立转向内部：你既是说话者，也是被反驳的那个人。

normal.en: Contradictory is the adjective of two arrows; contradiction is the second arrow itself.
normal.cn: contradictory 是两支箭的形容词；contradiction 就是第二支箭本身。

abstract.en: Picture one point with two arrows leaving it in exactly opposite directions. Only one of them can point where the truth is.
abstract.cn: 想象一个点射出两支方向完全相反的箭。只有一支能指向真相所在的方向。

abstract.en: The arrows can be two people, two reports, a claim and a record, or a theory and its data.
abstract.cn: 这两支箭可以是两个人、两份报告、一项主张与一份记录，或一个理论与它的数据。

abstract.en: Because the word means 'speak against', even a silent record 'speaks' when it contradicts a claim; English lends a voice to the evidence.
abstract.cn: 因为这个词本义是“反着说”，所以连沉默的记录在与主张冲突时也“说话”；英语把声音借给了证据。

examples.en: She contradicted the official account of the accident.
examples.cn: 她反驳了官方对事故的说法。

examples.en: The two witnesses contradicted each other.
examples.cn: 两名证人彼此的说法相互矛盾。

examples.en: His actions contradict everything he says about saving money.
examples.cn: 他的行为与他关于省钱的言论完全矛盾。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯·戳·迪克特”——肯（定）戳（穿）迪克特（dict 说）的话，把它反过来讲 → contradict 反驳、矛盾

root: 源自拉丁语 contra dicere“反着说”，由 contra“反对”+ dicere“说”构成，核心是“把一句话放到另一句话的正对面”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of contradict, all built on two arrows. A person, a rumour, one's own earlier words, a logical proposition, a record, an expectation — each can be placed opposite something that claims to be true.
sensesIntro.cn: contradict 的九个义项都建立在两支箭上。一个人、一则传闻、自己先前的话、一个逻辑命题、一份记录、一种预期——每一个都能被放到某个自称真实之物的对面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two arrows leaving one point in exactly opposite directions.
core.cn: 核心意象：两支箭从同一点射向完全相反的方向。

branches.en: SPEAKING AGAINST: a person denies or opposes what another has said, and the second voice is the answer.
branches.cn: 反着说：一个人否认或反对另一个人所说的话，第二个声音就是回答。

branches.en: FACTS AGAINST FACTS: two reports, or a version against a record — neither has a mouth, yet they clash.
branches.cn: 事实对事实：两份报告，或一种说法对一份记录——它们都没有嘴，却发生了冲突。

branches.en: TURNED INWARD: self-contradiction places both arrows inside one speaker.
branches.cn: 转向内部：自相矛盾把两支箭都放进同一个说话者体内。

branches.en: THE LOGICAL FORM: contradictory marks the relation, contradiction names the opposing statement, and logic uses it as a proof tool.
branches.cn: 逻辑形式：contradictory 标记关系，contradiction 命名那句相反的话，逻辑则把它当作证明工具。

branches.en: AGAINST THE EXPECTATION: a result can contradict the trend, standing out from the pattern everyone expected it to follow.
branches.cn: 与预期相反：一个结果可以与趋势相违，脱离众人预期它应遵循的模式。

intro.en: Contradict is contra- + dict- + -Ø. English adds -ion, -ory, -or and -able, and the broader dic- family keeps the 'say' meaning.
intro.cn: contradict 是 contra- + dict- + -Ø。英语加 -ion、-ory、-or、-able，而更广的 dic- 词族保留“说”的意义。

latinIntro.en: The Latin dicere family is very large: dicere, dictus 'said', contradictio, dictio 'a saying', praedicere 'foretell', and verdictum 'truly said'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dicere 词族非常庞大：dicere、dictus“说过的”、contradictio、dictio“说法”、praedicere“预言”、verdictum“如实说出”。

items.meaning: to speak against; to be inconsistent with
a statement that opposes another; the state of clashing
items.meaningCN: 矛盾；反驳；矛盾之处（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: There is a contradiction between the two clauses.
items.exampleCN: 两个条款之间存在矛盾。

items.meaning: mutually opposed; unable to be true together
items.meaningCN: 相互矛盾的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.exampleCN: 证人给出了相互矛盾的回答。

items.meaning: a person who contradicts or opposes
items.example: His main contradictor was the junior minister.
items.exampleCN: 他主要的反驳者是那位副部长。

items.meaning: able to be contradicted or denied
items.meaningCN: 可被反驳的（-able 表可能）
items.example: That claim is not easily contradictable.
items.exampleCN: 那个主张不容易被反驳。

items.meaning: the state of contradicting one's own words
to say what will happen before it happens
items.meaningCN: 预测；预言（pre- 表之前，同一词根）
items.example: Scientists predict a rise in sea level.
items.exampleCN: 科学家预测海平面会上升。

items.meaning: to say words for someone to write; to give orders
items.example: She dictated the letter to her assistant.
items.exampleCN: 她向助理口述了这封信。

items.meaning: the decision a jury gives, literally 'truly said'
items.meaningCN: 裁决（字面“如实说出”，同一词根）
items.example: The jury reached a verdict at noon.
items.exampleCN: 陪审团中午作出了裁决。

items.meaning: the choice and use of words; pronunciation
items.example: The poem's diction is deliberately old-fashioned.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗的措辞刻意古旧。

definition_zh: 矛盾；反驳；自相矛盾的说法
definition_en: a difference between two statements that cannot both be true, or the act of saying someone is wrong
core_image: 同一张纸上两句话各指相反方向，彼此顶住
scene: 他先说没去过，后来又描述那里的天气。There is a clear contradiction between his two answers.
sceneCN: 这里 contradiction 指「矛盾」（第 1 个义项：两句话不能同时为真）；句意是他的两个回答之间存在明显的矛盾。

pos.zh: 矛盾；反驳；自相矛盾的说法

senses.title: Two claims at odds
senses.definition: a state in which two statements cannot both be true
senses.definitionCN: 两句话不能同时为真的状态
senses.example: There is a contradiction between the two reports.
senses.exampleCN: 两份报告之间存在矛盾。
senses.why: Two arrows pointing opposite ways cannot share one target.
senses.whyCN: 两支反向的箭无法共用一个靶心。

senses.title: Speaking against
senses.definition: the act of saying that someone has said something wrong
senses.definitionCN: 指出某人说错了的行为
senses.example: His quiet contradiction surprised the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他平静的反驳让满屋人惊讶。
senses.why: A voice lifted against a claim is also a kind of answer.
senses.whyCN: 有人出声反对一个说法，也是一种回答。

senses.title: A self-defeating phrase
senses.definition: a combination of words whose parts cancel each other out
senses.definitionCN: 词语组合中两部分彼此抵消
senses.example: A silent alarm is a contradiction in terms.
senses.exampleCN: 无声的警报是措辞上的自相矛盾。
senses.why: Some word pairs fight inside their own sentence.
senses.whyCN: 有些词对在自己的句子里就打起架来。

intro.en: Contradiction comes from Latin contradicere, to speak against, built from contra-, against, and dicere, to say.
intro.cn: contradiction 来自拉丁语 contradicere（反着说），由 contra-（反对）与 dicere（说）构成。

items.en: Dicere meant to say or declare something.
items.cn: dicere 意为说出或宣称某事。

items.en: Contra meant facing or standing against.
items.cn: contra 意为面对着或站在对面。

items.en: Contradicere meant to speak against a claim.
items.cn: contradicere 意为对某种说法反着讲。

items.en: Contradictio named the state of two claims clashing.
items.cn: contradictio 指两种说法相冲突的状态。

items.en: French contradiction kept the clash of statements.
items.cn: 法语 contradiction 保留了说法相冲突之义。

items.en: English contradiction added the everyday sense of a mismatch.
items.cn: 英语 contradiction 增添了日常的不相符之义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin saying base dict-, and the meaning group names other words for a clash of claims.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的说话词基 dict-，近义组列出其他表示说法冲突的词。

entries.definition: to say that a statement is wrong
containing opposite ideas
a statement about what will happen
a serious difference between two things
strong disagreement with something
a statement that something is not true

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two claims pulling apart, then move to a voice raised against one claim and a phrase that cancels itself.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从彼此拉开的两句话开始，再到对一种说法发出的反对声，最后到自我抵消的短语。

normal.en: Contra- is against and dict is say, so contradiction is saying against.
normal.cn: contra- 是反对，dict 是说，contradiction 就是反着说。

normal.en: Two answers, one mouth, no way both are true.
normal.cn: 一张嘴，两个回答，不可能两个都真。

normal.en: A quiet no can still be a contradiction.
normal.cn: 一声轻轻的否定，也可以是一种反驳。

normal.en: An honest lie is a phrase at war with itself.
normal.cn: 诚实的谎言，是一个和自己打仗的短语。

normal.en: Where two statements cannot stand together, the word appears.
normal.cn: 两句话站不到一起的地方，这个词就出现了。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows leaving one bow in opposite directions.
abstract.cn: 想象两支箭从同一张弓上朝相反方向飞出。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet torn down the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸从中间被撕开。

abstract.en: Picture a sign that says enter and exit on the same arrow.
abstract.cn: 想象一块牌子，同一个箭头上写着进和出。

examples.en: There is a contradiction in his account of the night.
examples.cn: 他对那晚的叙述里有矛盾。

examples.en: The two rules stand in direct contradiction.
examples.cn: 这两条规则直接相抵触。

examples.en: Her calm contradiction silenced the meeting.
examples.cn: 她平静的反驳让会场安静下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 contradiction 记成 contra（反对）加 dict（说）：两句话互相反着说、彼此顶住，就是矛盾。

root: 源自拉丁语 contradicere（反着说），由 contra-（反对）与 dicere（说）构成，指两说相冲、反驳与自相矛盾。

sensesIntro.en: From two claims that cannot both stand, to a voice raised against one, and at last to a phrase that cancels itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从不能同时成立的两句话，到对其中一句发出的反对，最后到自我抵消的短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two arrows leaving one bow in opposite directions.
core.cn: 核心意象：两支箭从同一张弓上朝相反方向飞出。

branches.en: Two statements cannot both be true at once.
branches.cn: 两句话不能同时为真。

branches.en: A person may also speak against a claim.
branches.cn: 人也可以出声反对某种说法。

branches.en: A phrase can fight inside itself.
branches.cn: 一个短语能在自身内部打起架来。

branches.en: A clash of claims and a voice against it are neighbours.

items.meaningCN: 一种说法顶着另一种说法

items.meaning: to say the opposite of a claim
items.meaningCN: 说出与某说法相反的话

items.meaning: the way words are chosen and spoken

a formal decision spoken in court

definition_zh: 矛盾的；相互抵触的；爱反驳的
definition_en: involving, containing, or causing a contradiction; expressing opposite ideas; given to contradicting others
core_image: 两个箭头指向相反方向，彼此顶撞
scene: 这组词中，The two witnesses gave contradictory accounts of what happened.
sceneCN: 这里 contradictory 是「矛盾的」（第 1 个义项：包含矛盾的）；句意：两位目击者对所发生的事给出了相互矛盾的描述。图中可辨识物件：两个人、两个相反的箭头、法庭、证词。

senses.title: Involving a contradiction
senses.definition: containing or involving two statements that cannot both be true
senses.definitionCN: 包含两个不能同时为真的陈述的
senses.example: His explanation was contradictory and confusing.
senses.exampleCN: 他的解释自相矛盾，令人困惑。
senses.why: Latin dicere 'to say' + contra 'against': contradictory is 'said against', i.e., in conflict.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 dicere「说」+ contra「反对」：contradictory 是「对着说」，即冲突。

senses.title: Mutually opposed
senses.definition: so opposed that both cannot be true or possible at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 如此对立以至于不能同时为真或同时成立
senses.example: The two theories are contradictory.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个理论是相互矛盾的。
senses.why: Two things are contradictory when one asserts what the other denies.
senses.whyCN: 当一个断言另一个所否定的东西时，两者就是 contradictory 的。

senses.title: Given to contradicting others
senses.definition: tending to oppose or disagree with what others say
senses.definitionCN: 倾向于反对或不同意他人所说的
senses.example: He has a contradictory personality and always argues.
senses.exampleCN: 他性格爱唱反调，总要争论。
senses.why: A contradictory person speaks against others habitually.
senses.whyCN: 一个 contradictory 的人习惯性地对着他人说话。

senses.title: Conflicting with reality
senses.definition: conflicting with what is actually the case
senses.definitionCN: 与实际情况冲突的
senses.example: His claims are contradictory to the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 他的说法与证据相矛盾。
senses.why: Something is contradictory to the facts when it says the opposite of them.
senses.whyCN: 当某物说的与事实相反时，它就与事实 contradictory。

senses.title: Inconsistent within itself
senses.definition: containing parts that disagree with each other
senses.definitionCN: 包含彼此不一致的部分的
senses.example: The report was internally contradictory.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告内部自相矛盾。
senses.why: When a single source contains opposing statements, it is internally contradictory.
senses.whyCN: 当一个来源包含对立陈述时，它就是内部 contradictory 的。

senses.title: In logic, a contradictory proposition
senses.definition: in logic, a proposition that denies exactly what another asserts
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑学中，恰好否定另一命题所断言内容的命题
senses.example: 'Some S is P' and 'No S is P' are contradictories.
senses.exampleCN: 「有些 S 是 P」和「没有 S 是 P」是矛盾命题。
senses.why: In logic, contradictories cannot both be true and cannot both be false.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑学中，矛盾命题不能同真也不能同假。

senses.title: Impossible to reconcile
senses.definition: so different that they cannot be made compatible
senses.definitionCN: 如此不同以至于无法兼容的
senses.example: The two values are contradictory and cannot both be pursued.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种价值观相互矛盾，无法同时追求。
senses.why: Contradictory values pull in opposite directions and cannot both be satisfied.
senses.whyCN: 矛盾的价值观拉向相反方向，不能同时满足。

senses.title: Disagreeing loudly or habitually
senses.definition: characterized by habitual opposition in speech
senses.definitionCN: 以习惯性言语反对为特征的
senses.example: Her contradictory tone annoyed everyone at the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她动辄反驳的语气惹恼了桌上所有人。
senses.why: This sense stresses the manner of speaking against, not just logical conflict.
senses.whyCN: 此义强调对着说的方式，而不仅是逻辑冲突。

intro.en: Contradictory comes from Late Latin contradictorius, from contradicere 'to speak against'. The root is dicere 'to say', with contra 'against'.
intro.cn: contradictory 来自后期拉丁 contradictorius，源自 contradicere「对着说」。词根是 dicere「说」，前缀 contra「反对」。

items.en: dicere meant 'to say, speak, declare'. It is the root of many English words: dictate, predict, verdict, dictionary.
items.cn: dicere 意为「说、讲、宣告」。它是许多英语词的词根：dictate、predict、verdict、dictionary。

items.en: contra- means 'against'. contradicere is 'to speak against'.
items.cn: contra- 意为「反对」。contradicere 是「对着说」。

items.en: contradictus, past participle of contradicere, gave the stem used in English contradict.
items.cn: contradictus，contradicere 的过去分词，提供了英语 contradict 所用的词干。

items.en: contradictorius meant 'relating to contradiction'. It was borrowed into French and English.
items.cn: contradictorius 意为「与矛盾相关的」。它被借入法语和英语。

items.en: Contradictory entered English in the 15th century, first in logic and rhetoric.
items.cn: contradictory 在 15 世纪进入英语，最初用于逻辑和修辞。

items.en: Today it appears in logic, law, science, and everyday talk about conflict.
items.cn: 如今它出现在逻辑、法律、科学以及关于冲突的日常谈论中。

note.en: The first group shares dicere; the second contains near-synonyms for conflicting.
note.cn: 第一组共享 dicere；第二组是冲突的近义词。

entries.definition: to assert the opposite; the verb behind contradictory
entries.definitionCN: 断言相反；contradictory 背后的动词

entries.definition: a combination of opposite statements; the noun behind contradictory
entries.definitionCN: 相反陈述的组合；contradictory 背后的名词

entries.definition: to say before; pre- 'before' + dicere
not staying the same throughout; close to contradictory but less absolute
entries.definitionCN: 前后不一致的；接近 contradictory 但不那么绝对

entries.definition: in disagreement or opposition; a more general term than contradictory
entries.definitionCN: 不一致或对立的；比 contradictory 更通用

entries.definition: completely different; contradictory adds the idea that both cannot be true
entries.definitionCN: 完全不同的；contradictory 还包含两者不能同真的含义

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real word relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分和真实同族词。

normal.en: contra- 'against' + dicere 'to say': contradictory is speaking against, in conflict.
normal.cn: contra-「反对」+ dicere「说」：contradictory 是对着说，相冲突。

normal.en: contradict is the verb; contradictory is the adjective describing that conflict.
normal.cn: contradict 是动词；contradictory 是描述该冲突的形容词。

normal.en: predict says before; contradict says against; both use dicere 'to say'.
normal.cn: predict 向前说；contradict 对着说；都用 dicere「说」。

normal.en: self-contradictory means something disagrees with itself.
normal.cn: self-contradictory 意为某物与自己矛盾。

normal.en: In logic, contradictories are pairs that can't both be true or both be false.
normal.cn: 在逻辑中，矛盾命题是不能同真也不能同假的对子。

abstract.en: Think of two arrows pointing at each other and colliding head-on: that's contradictory.
abstract.cn: 想象两支箭对指着迎头相撞：这就是 contradictory。

abstract.en: Think of one person saying 'yes' while another says 'no' about the same thing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人说「是」而另一个人对同一件事说「否」。

abstract.en: Think of a scale tipping both ways at once — impossible, hence contradictory.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平同时向两边倾斜——不可能，因此是 contradictory。

examples.en: The witness gave contradictory testimony on two different days.
examples.cn: 证人在两天里给出了相互矛盾的证词。

examples.en: These two findings are contradictory and cannot both be correct.
examples.cn: 这两个发现相互矛盾，不可能都正确。

examples.en: His policy is self-contradictory: it promises both higher spending and lower taxes.
examples.cn: 他的政策自相矛盾：既承诺更高支出又承诺更低税收。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「康吹迪克特瑞」——康（con）师傅对着（contra）说（dicere）的人唱反调 → contradictory 矛盾的

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all mean 'speaking against': statements, theories, personalities, or logical propositions may be contradictory.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都表示「对着说」：陈述、理论、性格或逻辑命题都可能是 contradictory 的。

branches.en: LOGICAL CONFLICT: statements that cannot both hold.

branches.en: MUTUAL OPPOSITION: things so opposed they cannot coexist.
branches.cn: 相互对立：如此对立以至于不能共存的事物。

branches.en: OPPOSITIONAL PERSON: someone who habitually speaks against.
branches.cn: 唱反调的人：习惯性对着说的人。

branches.en: AGAINST EVIDENCE: claims that clash with the facts.

branches.en: LOGICAL CONTRADICTORY: a proposition that is the exact opposite.
branches.cn: 逻辑矛盾命题：恰好相反的命题。

latinIntro.en: Latin dicere 'to say' produced a large family: dictate, predict, contradict, verdict, dictionary, dedicate, indicate. The root appears as dic-, dict-, or dit-.

definition_zh: 相反的；对立的；固执的
definition_en: completely different from something, or unwilling to agree with others
core_image: 两条线朝相反方向延伸，永不相交
scene: 他说往北，另一个人偏说该往南，两人谁也不让。Contrary to the forecast, the day stayed dry.

senses.title: Opposite in fact
senses.definition: completely different from what is stated or expected
senses.definitionCN: 与所述或所预期完全不同
senses.example: Contrary to the rule, the door was left open.
senses.exampleCN: 与规定相反，门被开着。
senses.why: A fact that refuses the forecast must be said out loud.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝预报的事实，得被大声说出来。

senses.title: Set against
senses.definition: opposed in direction, nature or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 在方向、性质或目的上彼此相对
senses.example: The two plans pull in contrary directions.
senses.exampleCN: 两个方案朝相反方向用力。
senses.why: Two ropes on one load can only pull apart.
senses.whyCN: 同一重物上的两根绳，只会把东西拉开。

senses.title: Stubbornly opposed
senses.definition: willing to disagree just to have one's own way
senses.definitionCN: 为了照自己的意思而执意反对
senses.example: A contrary mood kept him silent all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 一股别扭劲儿让他整晚不说话。
senses.why: Some refusal has no reason beyond the wish to refuse.
senses.whyCN: 有些拒绝，除了想拒绝本身，别无理由。

intro.en: Contrary comes from Latin contrarius, opposite, from contra, against or facing.
intro.cn: contrary 来自拉丁语 contrarius（相反的），源于 contra（反对、面对）。

items.en: Contra meant facing something or standing against it.
items.cn: contra 意为面对某物或站在它的对面。

items.en: Contrarius described things placed on opposite sides.
items.cn: contrarius 形容被放在相对两侧的事物。

items.en: The word could also describe a person who always resists.
items.cn: 这个词也能形容总是顶着来的人。

items.en: French contraire kept both the spatial and personal senses.
items.cn: 法语 contraire 同时保留了空间与人的两层意思。

items.en: English contrary came to mean opposed in fact.
items.cn: 英语 contrary 逐渐指事实上的相反。

items.en: The phrase on the contrary became a fixed reply.
items.cn: 短语 on the contrary 成了固定的应答。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin against base contr-, and the meaning group names other words for what faces the other way.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的反对词基 contr-，近义组列出其他表示反方向的词。

entries.definition: a clear difference shown by comparison
to say that something is wrong
a nation with its own land and people
as different as possible from something
strongly disagreeing with something
going in the other direction

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a fact that refuses the forecast, then move to two forces facing apart and a will that refuses for its own sake.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从拒绝预报的事实开始，再到两股相对的力量，最后到为反对而反对的性子。

normal.en: Contra- means against, so contrary is the against word.
normal.cn: contra- 意为反对，contrary 就是那个反着来的词。

normal.en: Contrary to the plan, the day went another way.
normal.cn: 与计划相反，这一天走了另一条路。

normal.en: Two arrows from one point, pointing apart.
normal.cn: 从一个点出发的两支箭，指向两边。

normal.en: A contrary person argues before hearing the end.
normal.cn: 别扭的人还没听完就开始反对。

normal.en: On the contrary is the phrase that turns a sentence around.
normal.cn: on the contrary 就是让句子掉头的短语。

abstract.en: Picture two roads leaving one sign in opposite ways.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路从同一块路牌下朝相反方向走。

abstract.en: Picture a magnet pushing another away.
abstract.cn: 想象一块磁铁把另一块推开。

abstract.en: Picture a child crossing arms at a simple request.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子面对简单的请求抱起手臂。

examples.en: Contrary to expectations, the team won easily.
examples.cn: 与预期相反，这支队伍轻松获胜。

examples.en: The two accounts point in contrary directions.
examples.cn: 两种说法指向相反的方向。

examples.en: There is no evidence to the contrary.
examples.cn: 没有相反的证据。

sensesIntro.en: From a fact that refuses the forecast, to two forces facing apart, and at last to a will that refuses on purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 从拒绝预报的事实，到两股相对的力量，最后到存心反对的性子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two arrows leaving one point in opposite directions.
core.cn: 核心意象：两支箭从同一点朝相反方向飞出。

branches.en: The plainest sense says a fact goes the other way.
branches.cn: 最朴素的义项是说事实走了另一边。

branches.en: Two directions can be set against each other.
branches.cn: 两个方向可以彼此相对。

branches.en: A person may also take the opposite side for pleasure.
branches.cn: 人也会为了痛快而站到对面去。

branches.en: A broken forecast and opposing forces share one shape.
branches.cn: 落空的预报与相对的力量共用一个形状。

branches.en: Opposition in space turns into opposition in temper.
branches.cn: 空间里的对立变成了脾气里的对立。

intro.en: Contrary is built on Latin contra, against, plus the adjective ending -ary.
intro.cn: contrary 由拉丁语 contra（反对）加形容词词尾 -ary 构成。

latinIntro.en: The against base contr- also runs through contrast, contradict and controversy.
latinIntro.cn: 反对词基 contr- 也贯穿 contrast、contradict 与 controversy。

items.example: The result was contrary to plan.

a standing of two things side by side

items.exampleCN: 不要与自己的笔记相矛盾。

core_image: 黑白两块并排放着，边界格外清楚
scene: 展厅里两间屋子刷成一深一浅，站在门口就能看出差别。The contrast between the two rooms is striking.

senses.title: Side-by-side difference
senses.definition: a difference made clear by placing two things together
senses.definitionCN: 把两样东西并置之后显现出来的差异
senses.example: The contrast between the twins is obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 这对双胞胎的差异很明显。
senses.why: Two colours show their edge only next to each other.
senses.whyCN: 两种颜色只有并排时才显出边界。

senses.title: To set against
senses.definition: to compare two things in order to show how they differ
senses.definitionCN: 把两者放在一起比较以显出不同
senses.example: The report contrasts city life with country life.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把城市生活与乡村生活作对照。
senses.why: One picture explains another by standing beside it.
senses.whyCN: 一幅画靠着另一幅，就解释了它。

senses.title: A strong visual difference
senses.definition: the degree of difference between light and dark areas
senses.definitionCN: 明暗区域之间的差异程度
senses.example: Turn up the contrast on the screen.
senses.exampleCN: 把屏幕的反差调高一些。
senses.why: The eye reads edges before it reads shapes.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛先读边缘，再读形状。

intro.en: Contrast comes through French and Italian from Latin contra, against, and stare, to stand, so it first meant standing against.
intro.cn: contrast 经由法语和意大利语，来自拉丁语 contra（反对）与 stare（站立），本义是相对而立。

items.en: Stare meant to stand or stay in place.
items.cn: stare 意为站立或停在原处。

items.en: Contra stare meant to stand over against something.
items.cn: contra stare 意为站在某物的对面。

items.en: Contrasto named a quarrel and a facing of two sides.
items.cn: 意大利语 contrasto 指争执与两方对峙。

items.en: French contraste came to mean a striking difference.
items.cn: 法语 contraste 转指鲜明的差异。

items.en: English contrast was used for art and for argument.
items.cn: 英语 contrast 被用于绘画与论辩。

items.en: The word also names a dial on screens and cameras.
items.cn: 这个词也指屏幕和相机上的调节旋钮。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin standing base st-, and the meaning group names other words for difference and comparison.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的站立词基 st-，近义组列出其他表示差异与比较的词。

entries.definition: completely opposite to something
a formal written agreement
showing a difference between two things
the way in which things are not the same
the act of looking at two things together
the state of being against something

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two things placed near each other, then move to comparing them and to the sharp edge of light and dark.

normal.en: Contra- is against and st is stand, so contrast is two things standing face to face.

normal.en: Put black beside white and both look stronger.

normal.en: The noun is the gap, the verb is the act of showing it.
normal.cn: 名词是那道差距，动词是把它显出来的动作。

normal.en: A screen with more contrast hides the grey between.
normal.cn: 反差调高的屏幕，会藏起中间的灰。

normal.en: No second colour, no contrast.
normal.cn: 没有第二种颜色，就没有对比。

abstract.en: Picture two squares touching along one clean edge.
abstract.cn: 想象两个方块沿一条干净的边相接。

abstract.en: Picture a bright window in a dark wall.
abstract.cn: 想象深色墙上开着一扇明亮的窗。

abstract.en: Picture one hand open and one hand closed.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手张开，一只手握紧。

examples.en: The contrast between the two designs is clear.
examples.cn: 两个设计之间的对比很清楚。

examples.en: In contrast to last year, sales have risen.
examples.cn: 与去年相比，销售额上升了。

examples.en: The essay contrasts two ways of teaching.
examples.cn: 这篇文章对比了两种教学方式。

root: 源自拉丁语 contra（反对）与 stare（站立），经由法语和意大利语进入英语，本义是相对而立，后指对比与反差。

sensesIntro.en: From two things placed near each other, to the act of comparing them, and at last to the edge between light and dark.
sensesIntro.cn: 从并排放着的两样东西，到把它们比较的动作，最后到明暗之间的那道边。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black square laid against a white one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块黑方块紧贴着一块白方块。

branches.en: Nearness makes the difference visible.
branches.cn: 靠近让差异变得可见。

branches.en: The verb does the work of putting them side by side.
branches.cn: 动词负责把它们并排放好。

branches.en: Light and dark give the word a technical life.
branches.cn: 明与暗让这个词有了技术上的用法。

branches.en: A difference and the act of showing it belong together.
branches.cn: 差异和把差异显出来的动作分不开。

branches.en: Comparing and tuning both sharpen an edge.
branches.cn: 作比较与作调节，都是在磨利一条边。

intro.en: Contrast is built on Latin contra, against, plus stare, to stand.
intro.cn: contrast 由拉丁语 contra（相对）与 stare（站立）构成。

latinIntro.en: The standing base st- also appears in stable, statue and constant.
latinIntro.cn: 站立词基 st- 也出现在 stable、statue 与 constant 中。

items.meaning: to stand two things face to face
items.meaningCN: 让两样东西面对面站着

items.meaning: making a difference easy to see
items.exampleCN: 他们穿了对比鲜明的颜色。

items.meaning: to draw into a smaller space
to set two things beside each other
the act of setting things together
items.meaningCN: 把事物并置比较的行为

definition_zh: v. 违反，违背；与…相抵触
definition_en: to break a rule or go against something
core_image: 一只脚跨过写着禁止的横线
scene: 司机因违反停车规定被罚了款。The driver contravened the parking rules and was fined.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：contravene 指违反；句意是司机违反停车规定被罚款。

senses.title: Break a rule or law
senses.definition: to act against a rule or law
senses.definitionCN: 做出违反规定或法律的行为
senses.example: He contravened the parking rules.
senses.exampleCN: 他违反了停车规定。
senses.why: A foot stepping over a painted line.
senses.whyCN: 踩过警戒线的一只脚。

senses.title: Go against a principle
senses.definition: to act against a stated principle
senses.definitionCN: 做出与既定原则相反的事
senses.example: The order contravenes basic fairness.
senses.exampleCN: 这道命令违背基本公平。
senses.why: An arrow turned against its target.
senses.whyCN: 掉头背离靶心的箭。

senses.title: Be inconsistent with
senses.definition: to conflict with something stated
senses.definitionCN: 与所述内容相冲突
senses.example: The claim contravenes the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 该说法与证据相抵触。
senses.why: Two statements that cannot both stand.
senses.whyCN: 无法同时成立的两句话。

intro.en: Contravene joins Latin contra, against, to venire, to come.
intro.cn: contravene 把拉丁语 contra（反对）接到 venire（来）上。

items.en: Contra means against or opposite.
items.cn: contra 意为反对、相反。

items.en: Venire means to come.
items.cn: venire 意为来。

items.en: Contravenire means to come against.
items.cn: contravenire 意为前来相抗。

items.en: French contrevenir carried the legal sense.
items.cn: 法语 contrevenir 带有法律含义。

items.en: English used contravene of broken statutes.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语用它指违反法令。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the contra- start; the near-meaning group names breaking a rule.
note.cn: 形近组共享 contra- 开头；近义组都是「违反规则」。

entries.definition: The act of breaking a rule.
A usual practice or a meeting.
A clear difference.
To break a rule or right.
To break an agreement.
To break a law or right.
